scenes.narration: Some sounds hit you physically before you have even identified them. That reaction is older than language.
The auditory system connects directly to the amygdala, so a threatening sound can trigger a response before the cortex processes what it was.
Frequencies near a scream are especially potent because the brain is tuned to that specific band.
The frisson you get from music is a different mechanism. Unexpected chords and sudden dynamic shifts produce a measurable dopamine release.
Rhythm does the rest. Synchronized beats increase pain tolerance and produce a sense of shared attention even with strangers.
You are not being dramatic about the noise. Your hearing system is simply faster than your reasoning.
